Noah Brooks: Hey team, quick check: my kid was just added to my partner's insurance through their employer. Do I need to remove them from my Redwood coverage now or will coordination of benefits handle it?
People Ops: Coordinating benefits yes, but we recommend you remove them to avoid duplicate premiums. You have 30 days from the qualifying event (partner enrollment) to update our plan.
Noah Brooks: if i don't remove them right away, will the claims get denied?
Carla (Benefits): claims get coordinated; typically one plan is primary & the other secondary. But premiums are still charged on both plans unless you actively remove the dependent. If you're getting premium assistance through payroll, removing the dependent avoids paying for duplicate coverage.
Ian (Payroll): contact payroll@redwood.com to request retro refund for premiums paid after event if within audit window. We'll need proof of partner's coverage effective date.
Benefits Bot: Auto: docs required: partner coverage proof, signed QLE form, updated dependent docs. Submit within 30 days.
Noah Brooks: thanks, will submit.
